title: Signal Retro + Micro-OKR Playlet
body:
Context:
This is a compact weekly retro + micro-OKR planning scratch for my personal cadence. Aim is to keep a tight loop (3–5 signals) so I can iterate on habits and small experiments rather than bloated task lists. Not polished — notes to self, quick numbers, experiment ideas, and friction flags.

Top priority (northstar for next 2 weeks):
- Increase uninterrupted deep focus blocks to 10 hours/week (target) from current ~6.
- Push latency-cost experiment for local KV cache: target 12% p50 latency reduction on dev load test.

Signals I care about (tracked signals):
- Deep focus hours: 6 (last week) -> goal 10
- PR throughput: 3 merged (blocked by reviews)
- Oncall interrupts: 2 pageouts (both infra config flaps)
- Dev test latency (p50): 780ms -> target 690ms after cache experiment
- Personal wellbeing: sleep avg 6.5h/night

Quick retro (what worked / didn't):
- Worked: Blocking calendar for 90-min deep work twice a day was helpful on Wed/Thu.
- Didn't: Kept accepting short syncs; they fractured my focus.
- Surprise: Pausing notifications on Slack channel #infra-debug reduced context switching more than I expected.

Hypotheses / experiments (2-week micro-OKRs):
1) Focus Firewall
   - Hypothesis: If I enforce two 90-min focus windows daily + a 30-min midday buffer, I will hit 10 focus hours/week and complete 2 PRs.
   - Metric: deep_focus_hours >= 10, PRs_merged >= 4 by end of period.
   - Tasks: set Do Not Disturb auto from 10:00-12:00, 14:00-15:30; auto-decline external meeting invites in those blocks.
   - Risks: urgent pages during windows — fallback: allow oncall buddy to escalate only if SLO > 5 min.

2) Local KV cache pilot (dev only)
   - Hypothesis: Local per-worker KV cache reduces repeated prefix recompute and reduces p50 by >=12% on dev cluster.
   - Metric: p50_dev_request_latency drops from baseline (780ms) by 12%+, stable correctness tests.
   - Quick plan: prototype caching layer in feature branch, run small batch replay (2k requests) by Fri.
   - Blockers: need a quick perf harness; request help from Lina for harness infra.

3) Review hygiene sprint
   - Hypothesis: If I pair-review PRs twice a week and leave clear review comments, review turnaround will drop from avg 36h to <24h.
   - Metric: avg_review_turnaround < 24h.
   - Tactics: carve 3x30m slots for reviews, message team about lightweight review checklist.

Weekly plan (concrete):
- Mon: carve focus windows, triage backlog, schedule cache perf run with Lina.
- Tue: implement small cache shim, write basic unit tests (2h).
- Wed: run perf harness, collect metrics, draft short bug/follow-ups.
- Thu: pair-review block with Marcus, finalize PR.
- Fri: retro notes, update this doc, relax + catch up on learning (30m reading).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Is the dev harness representative enough? Need sample distribution from production traces (ask SRE).
- TODO: add lightweight checklist for PRs (5 bullets) — draft and share by Wed.
- TODO: ping Lina in #perf about timeslot availability.
- TODO: record my sleep + focus in a tiny spreadsheet to validate signal (start tonight).

Mini metrics table (manual, for quick glance):
- Baseline deep focus: 6h/week
- Target deep focus: 10h/week
- Baseline p50 latency: 780ms
- Target p50 latency: <= 690ms
- PRs merged baseline: 3/week
- Target PRs: 4/week

Notes to self: keep experiments small and reversible. If Focus Firewall causes too many missed discussions, reduce to single 90-min block and schedule an office hours slot. Write short blurb summarizing results at the end of the 2-week window and link to JIRA ticket for any follow-up work.

Links / quick refs:
- Draft perf harness (WIP): github.com/redwood-inference/perf/harness/kv-proxy (WIP)
- Review checklist (placeholder): https://confluence.redwood.ai/personal/pr-review-template
- Oncall runbook snippet: CON-OPS-382 (refer when gating focus windows)

Retrospective prompts for end of micro-cycle:
- Did I actually hit the focus hours target? If not, what broke the plan?
- Was the cache pilot measurable and stable? If yes, what's the minimal follow-up to run in staging?
- Which review habits stuck, which didn't?

Quick sign-off: Keep this doc tight. Update after each week with raw numbers (deep_focus_hours, PRs_merged, p50). If things go well, convert to a short playbook and share in growth-hours channel.
